newsitem.title: UK: Quiet LIFFE grains firm, consumer buying cited.
newsitem.headline: Quiet LIFFE grains firm, consumer buying cited.

text.p: LIFFE grain futures ended a slow day higher by up to 0.70 stg.
Consumer buying fuelled the rise, with shippers selling into it, one futures trader said. Futures had traded in a tight range all day.
A weaker sterling also helped the market.
Active May wheat last traded 0.60 stg up at 97.60 stg. May volume was 232 lots of a total 405 lots.
Barley volume was 20 lots, with 17 of them on March, which last traded unchanged at 92.00 stg.
One of the UK's biggest feed compounder buyers was highly sceptical about whether enough consumer interest could be found for the market's current strength to be maintained.
"The trade is trying to suck the end-user in, but the cover on for March is pretty high," he said.

Last Tuesday's jump demonstrated the phenomenon, which has been repeated several times, he said. Prices jumped and farm sellers, who are selling March, were enticed out into the market. But then futures had to be sold off again the following day as consumers failed to bite.
"The market pops up and farmers see a selling opportunity. The last five times the market moved up it got knocked back down again," he said.
What last week did do was jack up the range in which UK grain futures are operating by two to three sterling, he said.
The trade's new-found optimism on exports was misplaced, he said. "I would go against the feeling it's so tight," he said. "It's a struggle to see it so tight it will stay up", he said.
The south and East Anglia had had a good run on exports, but further north, in the Midlands, or Lincolnshire or Yorkshire there was a lot more grain still on farm, he said.
He was also betting on continued sterling strength. "We could come in tomorrow and see it at 2.75 or 2.76 against the mark and futures would come off a pound," he said.
